blocks.text: A kidney is a reddish-brown, bean-shaped organ with an adrenal gland on its top; the kidney and its adrenal gland are wrapped in a fibrous renal capsule. Each kidney has a convex side and a concave side. A depressed area on the concave side is the renal hilum (hilus), where the renal artery enters and the renal vein and ureter leave.

blocks.caption: Inside the kidney
rows: the outer portion, about a third of the kidney's mass
the inner portion, about two thirds, made of cone-shaped renal pyramids
a funnel-shaped space in the centre where urine collects before leaving through the ureter

blocks.alt: Left: the urinary organs from the front, two bean-shaped kidneys with adrenal glands on top beside the aorta and inferior vena cava, the right kidney a little lower, ureters running down to the urinary bladder in the pelvic cavity and the urethra below it. Right: a kidney cut open, showing the renal capsule, the outer cortex, the inner medulla with cone-shaped pyramids, the funnel-shaped renal pelvis, and the renal artery, renal vein and ureter at the hilum.
blocks.caption: Internal structure of the kidney (original diagram after Figure 14.2).
blocks.long_description: The urinary system is two kidneys, two ureters, one urinary bladder and one urethra. The kidneys lie high in the abdomen on either side of the vertebral column, between the 12th thoracic and 3rd lumbar vertebrae; the right one is a little lower and smaller because of the liver. Each ureter, about 25 cm long, starts at the renal pelvis and carries urine to the bladder, a stretchable muscular store in the pelvic cavity; the urethra takes urine out of the body. Inside the kidney the cortex makes about a third of the mass and the medulla, with its renal pyramids, about two thirds; urine collects in the renal pelvis and leaves through the ureter at the hilum, where the renal artery enters and the renal vein leaves.

blocks.text: Each kidney contains about one million microscopic tubes called nephrons, the functional units of the kidney. A nephron has two main parts, a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule.

items: Renal corpuscle: (i) the glomerulus, a network of capillaries derived from an afferent arteriole; (ii) Bowman's capsule, a cup-shaped, double-walled sac surrounding the glomerulus.

Renal tubule, leading away from Bowman's capsule: (i) the proximal convoluted tubule, the first, highly coiled part; (ii) the loop of Henle, a U-shaped hairpin whose descending limb runs towards the medulla and whose ascending limb returns towards the cortex, to lie beside the renal corpuscle; (iii) the distal convoluted tubule, coiled again, into which the ascending limb opens.

Collecting duct: the distal tubules of many nephrons drain into one collecting duct; as the ducts descend through the medulla they merge into larger papillary ducts, which empty into the renal pelvis.

blocks.caption: Two kinds of nephron
rows: start deep in the cortex, near the medulla
long, reaching deep into the medulla

blocks.alt: Left: one nephron across the cortex and medulla: a wide afferent arteriole enters the glomerulus inside Bowman's capsule and a narrower efferent arteriole leaves; the proximal convoluted tubule leads to the loop of Henle dipping into the medulla, the distal convoluted tubule returns beside the capsule and drains into a collecting duct; peritubular capillaries wrap the tubules and the vasa recta run beside the loop. Right: a flow chart of the blood route from renal artery to inferior vena cava.
blocks.caption: Structure of a nephron (original diagram after Figure 14.3).
blocks.long_description: A nephron has a renal corpuscle, the glomerulus (a capillary knot fed by an afferent arteriole) inside the double-walled Bowman's capsule, and a renal tubule: the coiled proximal convoluted tubule, the U-shaped loop of Henle with a descending and an ascending limb, and the coiled distal convoluted tubule, which drains with others into a collecting duct. Blood enters by the renal artery, passes into afferent arterioles, the glomerulus and the efferent arteriole, then the peritubular capillaries round the convoluted tubules and, in juxtamedullary nephrons, the vasa recta beside the loop, before venules and veins return it through the renal vein to the inferior vena cava. About 85% of nephrons are cortical with short loops; juxtamedullary nephrons have long loops deep in the medulla.
